title: Pricing entitlements, quotas & billing acceptance criteria for hosted/dedicated plans
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: Define and lock the product requirements for plan entitlements, runtime rate limits, monthly quotas, overage handling, and billing acceptance criteria for Redwood hosted API plans and Dedicated reserved tiers. This ticket is the canonical PRD for the Billing and Entitlements workstream for Q2.
description_long: Background: As part of the Pricing & Packaging Revamp, we need clear, enforceable rules and billing behaviors that: 1) allow product-led onboarding with free tier and predictable paid tiers; 2) enable Dedicated customers to reserve capacity with predictable cost; 3) provide transparent overage and proration rules; 4) support soft and hard quota enforcement models; and 5) produce auditable invoices and usage records for finance and customers. Goals: - Define per-plan entitlements (tokens, embeddings, concurrency, model tiers) - Specify runtime rate-limiter and quota enforcement semantics (soft vs hard) - Define overage billing rules, proration for plan changes, and credit/refund policies - Create acceptance criteria that the engineering and billing teams can validate before launch Scope: - Hosted plans (Free, Developer, Business, Enterprise) - Dedicated reserved capacity (S, M, L tiers) - Entitlements for streaming, chat, embeddings, and fine-tuned models - Runtime enforcement (rate limits, concurrency, per-minute/hour/day/month quotas) - Billing system integrations (invoicing, metering, Stripe/Billing connector) Out of scope: - Full marketplace invoicing flows, third-party reselling, tax rules beyond basic VAT collection. Stakeholders: - Product: Aisha Patel (owner), Evan Brooks (billing PM) - Engineering: Runtime & Billing (owners ENG-2384, ENG-2470) - Finance: Maria Lopez - Legal & Security: Claire Nguyen - Sales/CS: Priya Rao
requirements: Functional: Plan entitlements must be configurable by plan and include: monthly token allotment, embedding units, concurrent requests, sustained QPS, permitted model families (open, quantized, and Redwood-verified), and access to console features (rollouts, long-term retention).

Runtime behavior: Rate-limiter must enforce both per-minute and per-hour request rates; concurrency limit per API key must be enforced as a separate control; soft quota mode must provide 95th-percentile notifications then allow throttling after configurable grace; hard quota mode must block requests and return 402 Payment Required or 429 Too Many Requests depending on billing status.

Metering: All tokens and embedding units consumed must be recorded with model, sequence length, request_id, timestamp, and route tags for cost attribution. Usage events must be exportable to billing pipeline and retained for 365 days.

Overage: Paid plans may allow overage charging for tokens beyond monthly allotment. Overage rates must be configurable per plan and must cap monthly overage to a configurable percentage (default 200% of plan base revenue).

Proration: When customers upgrade or downgrade mid-cycle, token allotments and billing must be prorated by day with a transparent line-item on invoices. Downgrade that results in usage above new quota must trigger grace period and then enforcement per plan rules.
Notifications: Customers must receive email and console alerts at 70%, 90%, and 100% of quota and at 50%, 75% of projected spend over budget.
Audit & reconciliation: Billing records must reconcile to the metering dataset within 24 hours, and finance must be able to query raw usage for any invoice line item.

Dedicated: Reserved capacity customers should be billed on committed monthly price plus variable usage for burst if enabled. Dedicated entitlements include guaranteed throughput SLOs and separate quota buckets; overages on Dedicated should be billed as burst usage at a defined premium multiplier.
plan_entitlements: Free: 100k generation tokens/month, 50k embedding units/month, 5 concurrent requests, access to community models only, console access with 7-day telemetry retention, rate limit 60 req/min per API key.
Developer: 10M generation tokens/month, 1M embedding units/month, 20 concurrent requests, access to standard model catalog, 30-day telemetry retention, rate limit 600 req/min per API key.
Business: 100M generation tokens/month, 10M embedding units/month, 100 concurrent requests, multi-region access, 90-day telemetry retention, role-based access, rate limit 3000 req/min per org key.
Enterprise: Custom tokens & embeddings, dedicated support, private model upload enabled, long-term retention options, custom SLOs, SAML/SSO, and per-customer rate limits negotiated in contract.
Dedicated-Small: Monthly reserved commit with baseline throughput and quota equivalent to 200M tokens/month; burst allowed up to 2x at premium rate.
Dedicated-Medium: Reserved commit for 1B tokens/month with 1.5x burst cap.
Dedicated-Large: Reserved commit for 5B+ tokens/month with negotiable burst and regional isolation options.
rate_limits_and_quotas: Per-key per-minute and per-hour rate limiting for request counts and token rate. Default enforcement windows: 1 minute and 1 hour.

Concurrency: Hard cap on concurrent inflight requests per API key; requests arriving when concurrency cap reached must receive 429 with Retry-After header. Concurrency is independent from per-minute rate limits.

Soft vs Hard quotas: Soft quotas -> allow continued serving for an additional grace window (configurable per plan, default 72 hours) while emitting warnings and applying 10-25% throttling to non-critical routes. Hard quotas -> immediate blocking after threshold, respond with 402 Payment Required if billing delinquent, otherwise 429 for rate enforcement.
Burst policy: Plans may permit temporary burst above sustained QPS, tracked against a rolling 30-day buffer. Bursts are billed as overage when they exceed burst allowance.
Streaming sessions: Streaming token rate should be counted separately and subject to a streaming-specific per-minute token-rate cap to avoid head-of-line blocking for other requests.
overage_and_billing_rules: Overage calculation: Overage = max(0, consumed_units - plan_allotment) * overage_rate. For tokens, use per-1k-token price with model multipliers applied. Model-specific multipliers must be applied at metering time and recorded.

Invoice generation: Monthly invoices must include line items for plan base fee, proration adjustments, overage lines with per-day granularity, and credits for refunds. Invoices must be available in console and sent to billing contact by email within 48 hours of invoice close.

Proration: Upgrades prorated immediately: remaining days of current cycle credited toward new plan. Downgrades scheduled at cycle boundary unless customer requests immediate switch with pro-rated adjustment and potential immediate soft quota enforcement.

Failed payments: On payment failure, mark account as delinquent, send 3-step escalation emails (day 1, day 5, day 10), apply soft quota after day 5, and apply hard enforcement or suspend after day 14 unless payment succeeds. Suspension must not delete usage history.
Credits & refunds: Finance may issue discretionary credits; credits applied to next invoice unless explicitly refunded. Refunds must be manually approved with audit trail.
billing_acceptance_criteria: Metering accuracy: Sampled end-to-end test demonstrating metering accuracy within 0.5% against synthetic workload for token counts and model multipliers.

Enforcement correctness: Simulated accounts across Free/Developer/Business/Dedicated must demonstrate soft quota warning flows, hard quota blocking, and correct HTTP status codes (429 vs 402) in automated integration tests.
Proration testcases: Unit and e2e tests for upgrade/downgrade proration, with invoices showing correct credited amounts and resulting balance changes.

Invoice completeness: Generated invoice must include plan details, usage lines, per-line quantities, unit prices, applied multipliers, taxes (if enabled), credits, and final balance. Test invoice generation for 10 sample customers with varied usage.
Reconciliation: Billing pipeline must reconcile to metering dataset within 24 hours; end-of-month reconciliation report for sample customers must have zero missing usage entries.
Notifications: Emails and console alerts for quota thresholds must be delivered, and webhook notifications to CS systems must fire reliably in test harness.
Dedicated billing: Reserved capacity invoices must show committed fee, burst usage, and any overage with premium multiplier; test with at least one Dedicated customer simulation.
Auditability: For any invoice line item, finance should be able to query raw metering rows supporting that line item via a console link or export.
monitoring_and_rollout_plan: Canary: Roll entitlements enforcement to 5% of tenant traffic as canary with telemetry on 1-minute error rate, 429/402 counts, and metering delta.
Metrics: Expose metrics for: quota_used_percent, quota_overage_amount, soft_warning_emitted, hard_block_count, invoice_generation_success, metering_reconcile_lag.
Dashboards: Prebuilt console dashboards for Product/Finance/Eng showing high-level billing health and top overage customers.
Rollback: Feature flags to revert soft/hard enforcement per-plan; rollback plan includes emergency manual override to stop hard-enforcement within 15 minutes.
open_questions: Should streaming tokens be billed as separate unit type or counted as generation tokens with a streaming multiplier? Recommendation: separate streaming token bucket with streaming multiplier applied. Decision required from finance.
What is the default overage cap multiplier for small business customers? (Propose default cap of 200% of base monthly price).
Which events require immediate webhook to CS (e.g., account hitting 90%/100%) versus batched digest?
Edge case: How to handle model migration where model multipliers change retroactively? Proposal: do not adjust historical invoices; apply new multipliers prospectively.
